candidates.question: A player strips their last ship from a colony to join an encounter. Afterward, may their returning or warp-retrieved ships restore that now-empty location without a specific exception? If a required relocation has no existing colony anywhere to receive the ships, where do they go?
required_facts: Removing last ship immediately eliminates colony.
Ordinary returning/retrieved ships cannot use that abandoned location as an existing colony.
Required relocation with no colony goes to warp unless a specific exception applies.
source_references: Rulebook p13 Stripping a Planet of Ships
candidates.novelty: Q006 asks whether stripping is permitted and loses a colony, but does not ask subsequent relocation eligibility/no-colony destination.

candidates.question: Under the original rulebook, a special destiny card designates the offense itself as the defense. May that player instead try to drive out a foreign colony in their own system; how is the actual defending colony chosen and what happens to other colors there?
required_facts: Original rulebook permits driving out a foreign colony after a self-designating special, as after own color.
Offense chooses one player's foreign colony as defense in own system.
All other colonies are bystanders and unaffected.
contextual_background: This conditional is explicitly stated in the original core rulebook; it does not posit an expansion effect.
source_references: Rulebook p12 Driving Out Foreign Colonies
candidates.novelty: Tests the expressly printed special-card eligibility branch; Q004 asks own-color choices only.

candidates.question: Oracle and Sorcerer are the main players. Explain their complete card-selection and swapping sequence, including which card is faceup or facedown at each step and whether their sharing a Planning phase makes the effects simultaneous.
required_facts: Oracle acts before selecting its card, forcing Sorcerer to play faceup.
Oracle sees that card, then selects and plays its own facedown.
Only after both selections may Sorcerer switch encounter cards, before revealing Oracle's card.
The before/after-selection timings govern; not simultaneous merely because both are Planning.
source_references: Printed original Oracle and Sorcerer sheets
candidates.novelty: Explicit source interaction whose different within-phase timings change precedence; individual power questions do not ask this sequence.

candidates.question: When using Clone Wild, what happens to an artifact you play, may it be played again during the same encounter merely because it was retained, and what printed role/phase applies to the flare?
required_facts: May retain the artifact instead of discarding it.
Printed permission is to play it again during a later encounter, not repeated replay in the same encounter.
Any player; any phase, with artifact's own legal timing still relevant.
source_references: Rulebook p5 printed Clone flare illustration, Wild text and role/phase
candidates.novelty: Printed flare changes ordinary artifact discard destination and reuse timing; not asked by the general flare system or Clone alien power.

candidates.question: Using the classic Filch Wild flare, what items may you illicitly take and to where, when must the flare be revealed and when may it be zapped, what happens if caught, and what changes about the deck/discards after it is revealed?
required_facts: May illicitly take own ships from warp to colonies or cards from deck/discard even without entitlement.
Does not need reveal unless caught, then may be zapped.
If caught lose one ship to warp and return items caught filching.
Once revealed deck/discards placed next to user for access.
contextual_background: Only one of standard and classic Filch flare is used; any-phase/as-any-player printed usage.
source_references: Rulebook p5 printed classic Filch Wild illustration
candidates.novelty: Specific printed cheating/reveal/caught procedure absent from seed and Filch's normal alien power question.

rejected_or_pending.candidate: Both main players reveal Morph in an ordinary base encounter
rejected_or_pending.reason: Original rulebook explicitly says one Morph makes it impossible; expansion/component-duplication effects excluded. Preserve printed counterfactual in summary but do not invent a current-core effect to enable it.

Sheet only specifies reducing higher card by lower; literal no-higher reading exists but no explicit equality ruling or official FAQ answer found. Source adjudication records what publisher clarification would resolve.
